_comment: Canonical positionless-star cases, shared by the PHP, API and React suites.
25,342 stars in AT-HYG 4.0 have no usable parallax, so no distance and no x/y/z.
Inventing a position for them was deliberately removed (DATA-QUALITY-OUTLIERS): a
fabricated distance produced absolute magnitudes bright enough to sort to the top of
every result. The null is the honest answer, and every consumer has to handle it.
MAINTAINER DECISION, 2026-07-30 (NULL-COORDINATES): a positionless star stays
FINDABLE in search but is INERT — no click-through to the map, never plotted, and the
result must say why it cannot be mapped. Hiding 25,342 real catalog stars was
rejected; so was a full 'unmapped' detail view, as more UI work than it is worth.
MEASURED FACTS THE IMPLEMENTATIONS RELY ON (2026-07-31, whole catalogue):
- dist and x/y/z always travel together. 0 stars have one without the other, in
either direction. One hasPosition() helper is therefore sufficient.
- Positionless stars have NO absmag but DO have an apparent mag. Since every search
orders by absmag ASC NULLS LAST, they always sort last and can never displace a
real result inside a limit.
- All of them carry a Tycho-2 id and a constellation; 116 have a HIP number.
NOT THE SAME THING: 1,222 stars have coordinates beyond MAX_COORDINATE_VALUE. Those
are unmappable for a different reason and stay excluded from search — they have an
absurd absmag that sorts them FIRST, which is what caused a 503. Do not merge the two
cases into one 'unmappable' concept.

cases.name: no position at all — the ordinary case
cases.why: no usable parallax, so no distance and no coordinates

cases.name: positionless star that also has a proper name
cases.why: a quasar carried as a stellar entry; the only positionless star with a proper name

cases.name: ordinary star with a full position
cases.why: the control case — must remain fully mappable

cases.name: star at the origin is positioned, not positionless
cases.why: 0.0 is a real coordinate. The bug being fixed cast null to 0.0 and drew positionless stars here, so a helper that confuses the two would reintroduce it exactly.
